title: Dark skies above the Atacama
caption: The Milky Way rising over the Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: The faint, diffuse glow of the Milky Way, only just visible among a sea of stars, rises from behind distant peaks in Chile's Atacama Desert. In the foreground, a desert road and the plants around it are lit by a weak red lamp.

Red light is often used at night by astronomers and photographers because it disturbs dark-adapted eyes less than white light. It picks out the road and the vegetation without washing out the sky above.

The Milky Way is our own galaxy, seen from inside its disc, where the light of distant stars blends into a soft band. It is just emerging from behind the mountains, so only part of its glow is on show. The photograph is by Carlos A. Durán.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera in the Atacama Desert. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers more light than the eye, so the Milky Way may appear more distinct here than it would in person, though the caption notes it is only just visible.
